Formulation  
A previously well male patient developed progressive fatigue, generalized aching, and reduced energy approximately six weeks ago, beginning a few weeks after returning from a holiday in the United States. There are no significant infectious symptoms reported, aside from a transient sore throat and a non-itchy rash on the calf, suggestive of possible tick-borne illness such as Lyme disease. Past medical history includes asthma and hay fever without recent flare-ups. Psychologically, patient reports good mood and stress levels but reduced concentration and energy consistent with his physical illness. Social support is stable with his wife. Work attendance has continued but effectiveness possibly affected by symptoms. Investigations including blood tests are planned to identify treatable infectious or other causes.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Persistent fatigue, body aches, and reduced energy  
- Patient Goal(s): Improve energy levels and physical wellbeing; identify underlying cause of symptoms  
- Clinical Goal(s): Rule out underlying infections (including Lyme disease) and other medical causes contributing to symptoms; optimize management accordingly  
- Actions (Patient): Attend for recommended blood tests; report any new or worsening symptoms; participate in follow-up consultation  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange blood tests including screening for Lyme disease and relevant routine labs (liver, kidney function, blood count); review results and provide treatment if indicated; follow up via telephone approximately 1 week after tests; monitor mental health and physical symptoms  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes; discussed possible infectious causes including Lyme disease, need for investigations, expected management  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: No specific signs recorded; patient advised to report any new symptoms
